subject: CloudSage: inference validation — prioritizing A/B bench tests and p99 gating
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Ross <matthew.ross@cloudsage.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: CloudSage: inference validation — prioritizing A/B bench tests and p99 gating

Hi Matthew / Amina,

Thanks again for the call today — good conversation and appreciate the clarity on the three primary success criteria from the CloudSage product team (latency p95/p99, steady-state tokens/sec per GPU, and tail-regression risk). Per ask from your side, I captured a prioritized lab plan and the immediate asks so we can get a deterministic A/B comparison with the hyperscaler endpoints you mentioned.

Summary of what CloudSage needs from Redwood to run the eval:
- A reproducible A/B harness that can hit both Redwood inference endpoints and the two hyperscaler-managed endpoints you shared (us-west endpoints).
- Test vectors: 3 workload classes (short chat prompts ~50 tokens, mid-length Q&A ~250 tokens, long context summarization ~2k tokens).
- Metrics: median latency, p95, p99, token/sec (steady state), and failed-request/error-rate.
- Clear measurement windows (e.g., 10-minute steady windows after warmup) and seed traffic patterns.

Proposed next steps (we can turn these into a mutual action plan if you like):
1) We will deliver a lab test matrix by EOD Monday (attached will be redwood-bench-matrix-v1.xlsx) that maps workloads to test duration and concurrency targets.
2) CloudSage provides the exact hyperscaler endpoint URLs and any auth tokens you want us to use for parity runs.
3) Rishi will own the actual run execution on Redwood side and share raw logs + p95/p99 plots.
4) Grace will coordinate measurement definitions and ensure KV-cache and batching knobs are aligned across runs (we'll document any differences).

Open questions we captured on the call (please confirm):
- For p99 gating, do you want absolute thresholds (e.g., p99 < 300ms) or relative delta vs hyperscaler (e.g., within 20%)?
- Should we include a quantized model variant (8-bit) as a fall-back in the A/B set?

Attachments: redwood-bench-matrix-v1.xlsx (test matrix stub), CloudSage_Security_QA.pdf (security questions you provided).

I'll follow up with the spreadsheet and a suggested run calendar. Thanks — Neha

--
Neha Kapoor

Redwood Inference

From: Matthew Ross <matthew.ross@cloudsage.com>

Cc: Amina Patel <amina.patel@cloudsage.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudSage: inference validation — prioritizing A/B bench tests and p99 gating

Neha — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications so the lab runs are apples-to-apples: 

- For p99 gating: prefer relative delta vs our current hyperscaler baseline. We want Redwood to show <15% delta at p99 for our short and mid workloads; for long-context jobs p99 tolerance is up to 25% given queueing differences.
- Please include the 8-bit quantized variant only if Redwood can run it behind the same API surface (we want runtime parity; operator-visible flags are OK but no separate end-point).
- We'll upload test tokens and the three workload templates to the Drive link you listed by EOD today. Also attaching a short doc with our baseline numbers (baseline-p99.csv).

One ask on reporting: can the results include both absolute latency distributions and a latency-per-token curve (so we can see how tokenization interacts with p99)? If you can include a short summary paragraph that calls out where Redwood outperforms hyperscalers (and where it doesn't), that will help the internal presentation.

Schedule: can Redwood run an initial parity pass the week of July 5? If so, we'll lock in a 2-hour window (steady-state) and provide the hyperscaler keys.

Thanks — Matt

--
Matthew Ross
Senior Platform Engineer
CloudSage Inc.
matthew.ross@cloudsage.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Ross <matthew.ross@cloudsage.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudSage: inference validation — prioritizing A/B bench tests and p99 gating

Thanks Matt — quick operational note and our proposed test matrix tweaks.

Operational plan (short):
- Warmup: 10 minutes at 30% target concurrency to fill KV caches and establish steady JIT/kernels.
- Measurement window: three 10-minute windows per workload class separated by 5 minutes cooldown. We'll report median/p95/p99 + tokens/sec aggregated per window.
- Error handling: any run with >1% 5xx/timeout will be flagged and re-run after triage.

Proposed tweaks to your asks to improve signal/noise:
- For the long-context (~2k tokens) workload we recommend measuring two modes: (A) contiguous streaming decode (typical Redwood path) and (B) chunked summarize (user-side chunking). The latter is how some hyperscaler runs are implemented and would explain some throughput differences.
- Include a synthetic microburst test (1s spike to 5x concurrency) to show p99 tail behavior under bursty traffic — this tends to surface queuing-induced p99s that get smoothed in steady-state windows.

Deliverables we will post to the Drive after the initial parity pass (ETA July 6):
- raw-logs.tar.gz (per-request timing + status)
- p99_plots.png (per-workload)
- token_rate_table.csv
- short-readme.md (test harness config + flags used)

I've attached an initial run calendar below (stub) and put the redwood-bench-matrix-v1.xlsx through the test-matrix adjustments (I added microburst rows). If the CloudSage team can confirm the hyperscaler endpoints and upload the baseline CSVs this week, we can aim for the July 6 delivery.

--

Subject: Re: CloudSage: inference validation — prioritizing A/B bench tests and p99 gating

Appreciate the rapid turnaround and the detailed plan. Confirming:
- We'll share the hyperscaler endpoint URLs and auth keys by close of day today (internal approvals cleared).
- Baseline numbers uploaded to your Drive folder: baseline-p99.csv and baseline-tokenrates.csv.
- July 6 initial parity window works for us — please reserve the 14:00-16:00 PDT slot.

Two small asks before the run: 1) can Redwood include a small sanity check that p95/p99 reporting is done with and without streaming enabled? We found discrepancies in earlier benchmarks from other vendors. 2) If possible, please include a single-line outcome recommendation after the run (e.g., "Recommend Redwood for short-chat workloads; evaluate quantized path for long-context"). That will speed internal sign-off.

See you in the run — Amina

--
Amina Patel
Product Lead, Model Platform
CloudSage Inc.
